svg.text: 02-Timeline. st_tx_video_session.c: Redundant P+R Link Drop & Wedged E610 Ring (Before vs. After)
ST 2022-7 dual-leg TX video session (P + R). Time axis is non-linear: "//" marks a cut. Source: lib/src/st2110/st_tx_video_session.c (15e2f411..c5f235c3).
PANEL A — BEFORE (base 15e2f411): P Loses Link & Returns With Wedged E610 Ring -> Fatal Cascade Kills P + R
P: dead TX ring still traps mbufs
R: UP (healthy link, but starved as P ring stalls)
R: flushed blindly during P recovery
Keeps feeding both legs (no resync / drain)
P fills TX ring -> reclaim stalls -> R starves too
No packets built on P or R
P ring holds chain mbufs -> sh_info stuck
All frame slots lock up; no sh_info retirement
Dead P ring keeps DMA ptrs
Crash risk on later port stop
No pool parking, no atomic swap; in_use > 0 as long as P ring is wedged
Both P and R permanently dead!
Outcome (BEFORE): A single-leg link bounce with a wedged E610 ring stalls R, fails tv_mempool_free() with -EBUSY, and kills the entire redundant session.
PANEL B — AFTER (PR #1951 HEAD c5f235c3): Link Resync/Drain, sh_info[4] Retirement & Atomic Pool Renew
P: dead txq swapped -> new txq
R: UP (pre-resync ring drains by t=152ms)
R: UP — streams FULL RATE during whole P outage!
Zero UAF on wedged P ring
No fatal error fired while P is down or draining; R streams uninterrupted on Gen 0; mbuf_mempool_parked[16] empty.
App thread reads pools via __ATOMIC_ACQUIRE in st20/st22_tx_get_mbuf() (never observes NULL).
Outcome (AFTER): R streams full rate throughout P's outage; wedged P queue recovers cleanly via sh_info[4] retirement + atomic tv_mempool_renew(), and parked pools reap after 1 s.

g.text: Link UP but E610 TX ring wedged
